surfaces.summary: Protocol v1 dirty-anchor bootstrap exception: a registry of exact tool definitions allowed to cross a session-wide dirty denial. WorkspaceLease v2 denies only the anchor repository, so the registry granted nothing and the guard never consulted it.

replacement.contract: agent-hook workspace-lease v2 anchor-local denial (dsh-runtime-kit.workspace-lease.v2); recovery through workspace_recovery and workspace_recovery_handoff over agent-hook workspace-recovery

surfaces.compatibility_window: none; a bundle that still calls the registry fails at boot with a missing method, which is the intended typed signal that it targets an unsupported runtime-kit
surfaces.rollback: reinstall the issue 79 acceptance package 4b21c79c3dda7e4715755a867fed2ad833f4a8f1f2c3d593eb7fcfcf45cff6dd through the digest-reviewed rollback operation

surfaces.summary: Deterministic in-memory artifact provider shipped inside the package although only the conformance tests constructed it.

replacement.contract: test/helpers/memory-artifact-provider.mjs (test-only); production uses LocalArtifactProvider under the session-owned ArtifactService

surfaces.compatibility_window: none; the provider was never a public export

surfaces.summary: The runtime-core health probe spawned agent-docs --version and matched the banner after it had already authenticated the executable byte-for-byte against the released digest.

replacement.contract: native runtime health readAuthenticatedBinary sha256 snapshot of agent-docs from compatibility/nils-cli.json (issue 58)

surfaces.compatibility_window: none; the digest check is stricter than the banner

surfaces.summary: Runtime-kit authored the remediation text for a blocked unsafe-default-delivery shape. nils-cli 1.27.37 supplies decision.context for the shell-classification denials (invalid command, unclassifiable command, unclassifiable shell state) and runtime-kit now promotes any context it receives ahead of its own text for every blocked shape; the lone unsafe-default-delivery remediation stays runtime-kit text until a nils release carries context for that code, which the same precedence promotes without a runtime-kit change.

replacement.contract: src/policy/nils-transport.js promotes agent-hook decision.context (shell-classification denials in nils-cli 1.27.37) ahead of the retained unsafe-default-delivery fallback text

surfaces.compatibility_window: runtime-kit remains the owner of the block-unsafe-default-delivery remediation text until nils-cli carries decision.context for that code

surfaces.summary: workspace_recovery told the model to restart the session as the default outcome of a dirty anchor; under v2 the denial is local to the repository and the wording now says so.

replacement.contract: agent-hook workspace-recovery inspect and handoff; WorkspaceLease v2 anchor-local denial

surfaces.summary: The minimum supported nils-cli release moves from 1.27.17 to 1.27.37, the release that contains every native contract the accepted children require; older companions fail typed before activation. compatibility/nils-cli.json declares the floor, src/operations/index.js applies it to agent-docs doctor, and src/acceptance/contract.js requires the accepted nils release to be at least the floor.
surfaces.compatibility_window: 1.27.37 only; agent-docs outside the range is reported as needs-attention and activation refuses
surfaces.rollback: reinstall the issue 79 acceptance package 4b21c79c3dda7e4715755a867fed2ad833f4a8f1f2c3d593eb7fcfcf45cff6dd, whose floor is 1.27.17

surfaces.summary: The legacy-pending-recovery-unsupported refusal was spelled twice; one helper owns it.
Normative documents described DSH rc.7 and rc.8 behaviour by release name; they now describe the supported rolling window, and docs/migration.md is fenced as history.
The nils-backed finish-line stop evaluator that runs when no authoritative acceptance contract governs the session.

replacement.contract: agent-hook finish-line stop (finish_line.rs) today; authoritative acceptance displaces it only for sessions a trusted consumer registered

surfaces.compatibility_window: retained until a child makes acceptance registration mandatory
surfaces.rationale: Issue 59 accepted authoritative acceptance as inert until a trusted consumer registers a contract, and the shipped bundle registers none, so this evaluator is the documented turn-stop path for every ordinary deployment. It is nils-authoritative (client.stop), not model-side evidence assembly. Making registration mandatory is a new contract for a new Gate 0, not a removal.

surfaces.summary: The declared operations-state-v1-to-v2 migration and its legacy readers.
surfaces.compatibility_window: one release: profiles written by runtime-kit before issue 64 migrate exactly once
surfaces.rationale: The closeout's own acceptance requires upgrade from the last legacy-compatible version to preserve supported state; this migration is that path and is declared in the lifecycle manifest, so the engine would refuse a manifest that dropped it.
Documented public surface with exact ref pairing; the live diagnostic path uses denialState, but removing a documented API is a contract change, not glue removal.

surfaces.summary: dataPolicyOpaqueTools embedder configuration that classifies named tools as opaque references for the typed data policy.
surfaces.rationale: The default bundle does not set it, but it is embedder-facing configuration exercised by the plugin contract tests, not a shadow fallback.

surfaces.summary: Advisory reminder rules in policy/dsh-runtime-kit-v1.toml (memory-write-principle-reminder, skill-usage-reminder, stop-pre-pr-reminder, forge-label-reminder).
surfaces.compatibility_window: kept while the nils hook-rules manifest lists them
surfaces.rationale: The DSH policy is verified 1:1 against the nils hook-rules manifest; retiring a rule is a nils-cli decision that then flows through the parity projection.

surfaces.summary: The reviewer wave's JavaScript worker pool and role-set classification alongside the host restricted-role registry's own capacity and role receipts.

replacement.contract: native-execution-boundaries-v5 restricted-role registry (registerRole, startRole, roleOf, configureRoleCapacity)

surfaces.compatibility_window: retained until a child consolidates capacity on the host receipts
surfaces.rationale: The registry is already the only admission and capacity authority; the pool only orders dispatch within the bundle's wave. Removing it changes concurrency semantics pinned by accepted tests and is a behaviour change for a later child.

surfaces.summary: Per-lane liveness sidecar and private checkpoint JSON written by the Main Agent orchestration.

replacement.contract: producer contract read by nils-cli session_status; session-owned ArtifactService for later consolidation

surfaces.rationale: The sidecar is a producer contract that nils-cli reads, not model-side bookkeeping; moving its path ownership into session-owned artifacts is a cross-repository contract change.

surfaces.summary: src/compat/dsh-rc7.js keeps the name of the release that introduced the seam although it adapts the whole supported rolling window (adapter identity dsh-rolling-v1).
surfaces.rationale: No rc.7-conditional branch exists; the name is vocabulary. A rename touches fourteen call sites and tests without changing behaviour and is excluded as unrelated refactoring.

surfaces.summary: The Agent Console profile pins one exact DSH release and TUI artifact rather than the three-release window.
surfaces.compatibility_window: intentionally narrower than the headless window
surfaces.rationale: The UI boundary is documented as exact; widening it requires TUI validation on every release.

surfaces.summary: native-execution-boundaries-v5 ships byte-identical patch files for alpha.4 and rc.1.
surfaces.rationale: The apply/reverse lifecycle authenticates one artifact per pinned release; sharing a file would couple two release lifecycles and is not glue removal.
